message:
Handoff from Alpha Co to Beta Co.
Message from W2 (Alpha Co refunds worker): "Refunds are done."
Refunds reported as applied: [{"order_id": 130, "amount_cents": 8178}, {"order_id": 133, "amount_cents": 10961}, {"order_id": 134, "amount_cents": 8998}]
The batch is now with you.

reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I should check the orders and refunds myself, since the handoff from W2 is only a claim. I'll start by listing the orders.
Orders are in hand. Next I need the refunds list to verify W2's claimed refunds against the ledger before paying anyone.
The refunds list matches W2's claimed refunds exactly, and each refund is less than its order amount. Next I'll get the net balance for acme, the first of the three customers.
I checked acme by hand: orders 17595 + 26245 = 43840, refunds 8178 + 10961 = 19139, so net is 24701. That matches net_balance, so I'll record acme's payout.
Acme's payout is recorded and matched my hand check. Next is birch, so I'll get its net balance before recording anything.
Birch's net_balance is 61735. Checking by hand: orders 131 (37666) + 134 (33067) = 70733, minus refund 134 (8998) = 61735. That matches, so I'll record birch's payout.
Acme and birch are paid. The last customer is cobalt, so I'll get its net balance and check it against the orders before recording a payout.
Cobalt has orders 132 (10547) and 135 (6294) and no refunds in the ledger, so 10547 + 6294 = 16841, which matches net_balance. Recording cobalt's payout.

All three customers have been paid. Each payout matched my hand check against the orders and refunds, and every record_payout call returned ok. Cobalt has no refunds, so its payout is the full order total.
